messages.subject: Pre-release of poppr version 2.1.1
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm planning on releasing poppr version 2.1.1 next week and I wanted to make sure that nothing breaks for anyone.

Details can be found on GitHub: https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/issues/89. As always, you can install it with devtools:

devtools::install_github("grunwaldlab/poppr", build_vignettes = TRUE)

Please comment on GitHub if you see anything that needs to be changed.

- Zhian

messages.subject: amova poppr
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have an error when trying to perform an amova with poppr. I am sending a job to a remote computer and I obtain this error message.

*** caught segfault ***
address 0x2b9b2f42d948, cause 'memory not mapped'

Traceback:
 1: vapply(x, function(x) .Call("pairdiffs", x@tab)/2, numeric(np))
 2: diss.dist(clonecorrect(x, strata = NA), percent = FALSE)
 3: poppr.amova(genind_object, ~V1, clonecorrect = FALSE, within = FALSE,     missing = "ignore")
aborting ...
./AMOVA_poppr_ignore.sh: line 5: 12633 Segmentation fault      (core dumped) Rscript AMOVA_poppr_ignore.R input1.txt input2.txt output.txt

Do you know why I am having this error?  I guess that it might be due to the size of the matrix? My data has 320 individual and ~85000 snps.

Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] amova poppr
messages.body_plain:
Hi Carles,

You appear to have sufficiently recent versions of the software, It seems that the issue appears to be with the distance function, but unfortunately, I can't tell what the cause may be. Basically, this is looping over each locus, calculating the distance, and then summing all of those up, so memory really shouldn't be an issue.

Since you are setting within = FALSE, you could try supplying your own distance matrix (this will calculate euclidean distance):

genind_dist <- dist(genind_object)
poppr.amova(genind_object, ~V1, clonecorrect = FALSE, within = FALSE, dist = genind_dist, missing = "ignore")

Zhian

I know that by default poppr.amova computes the diss.dist between pairs of individuals (allele differences between the two genotypes), but I don't understand how it works in the case of the Euclidean distance (how we could obtain a numeric euclidean distance from the alleles of the genotypes? Is it something intrinsic of the genind object?)

Thanks

Carles

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] amova poppr
messages.body_plain:
All you really need for amova is a distance matrix and a data frame of hierarchical levels (this is how it's implemented in both pegas and vegan). The missing options in poppr are simply for pre-processing the data before obtaining the distance matrix. The dist() function ignores missing data by default.

Regarding how the dist function works on genind data: the genind object represents data as counts of alleles, so the euclidean distance is based off of those counts.

Additionally, considering how many loci you have, you may want to consider placing your data in a genlight object and creating the distance matrix via bitwise.dist(). You can then use this with the pegas or vegan version of AMOVA.

Zhian

messages.subject: Re: NaN in eMLG SE estimation
messages.body_plain:
Ok I see this in Data import and manipulation in poppr version 2.1.1
"One thing to note about this output is the NaN in the column labeled SE. In R, NaN means “Not a num- ber”. This is produced from calculation of a standard error based on rarefaction analysis. Occasionally, this calculation will encounter a situation in which it must attempt to take a square root of a negative number. Since the root of any negative number is not defined in the set of real numbers, it must therefore have an imaginary component, i. Unfortunately, R will not represent the imaginary components of numbers unless you specifically tell it to do so. By default, R represents these as NaN"

So how do I get an actual value, instead of NaN?

messages.body_plain:
Hi Monique,

I'm not sure what could be causing this. The value of eMLG is calculated by the vegan package using the function "rarefy". You'll notice that this behavior happens with other data sets as well. I'm noticing that it's happening when you have unique MLGs in the population. If you look at the manual for diversity indices in vegan, it talks about why this is happening: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/vegan/vignettes/diversity-vegan.pdf
